statements.impact_statement: The Marvin attack is a timing sidechannel in RSA decryption and signing, which leaks PRIVATE-key operations. The `rsa` crate reaches this graph only through `pgp` 0.20, which the instrument uses to VERIFY detached OpenPGP signatures on version content (RM common master06 §Digital Signature): a verification-only path over public keys. The instrument holds no RSA private key and performs no RSA decryption or signing, so there is no secret for the sidechannel to leak. No fixed release exists upstream; the deleting event is the rsa 0.10 release, taken the day it ships (deny.toml carries the same adjudication as the gate).

The advisory reports timing variability in `crypto-bigint` operations meant to be constant-time, which leaks SECRET integers. `crypto-bigint` 0.5.5 reaches this graph only through `pgp` 0.20's `elliptic-curve` 0.13 stack (ecdsa, p256, p384, p521, k256) and `cx448`, and `pgp` 0.21 still requires `elliptic-curve` ^0.13. The signature judge verifies detached OpenPGP signatures over PUBLIC keys only. The run-record signer reads every secret key packet's algorithm before the key is parsed and refuses any component that is not RSA, Ed25519, legacy EdDSA, X25519 or Curve25519 ECDH, so no ECDSA, NIST or Brainpool ECDH, X448 or Ed448 secret scalar is ever decoded. RSA uses `num-bigint-dig` and the 25519 algorithms use `curve25519-dalek`, neither of which depends on `crypto-bigint`. Deleting event: OpenPGP signing removed by #593, or a `pgp` release on `elliptic-curve` 0.14 / `crypto-bigint` 0.7.6 or later (deny.toml carries the same adjudication as the gate).
